item.description:
• The WC is a WC: a pedestal, a seat at sitting height with the hole marked, the tank on its back with a button, square to the walls where the four-sided bowl read as a diamond; the sitter sits square on it facing out from the tank, and its shadow goes onto the seat with it instead of staying on the spot. The shower's arm comes off a pole up the corner wall with a tap at waist height, and a towel hangs over a rail on the other wall
  • The bubble's picks work by hand: the hover holds over a column from the minion's feet up to the plate, so the mouse can leave the body for the icons without the bubble going; a pick closes the bubble and lets the hover go, so the minion sets off at once; sent to bed from the bubble, a minion lies down once on its bunk whatever its session is up to, a nap flag on the body cleared by the next send elsewhere
  • Walkers never stop for anybody: someone in the way is passed a third of a tile to the walker's own right, and within a sidestep of the waypoint the pass counts as done, since the bearing to a near waypoint swings and the spot beside it can never be chased to the point. The whole step is Walk.step, SceneKit-free; --walk-tests has two on one spot heading the same way, opposite ways, and a follower, all arriving. The idle soak passes three times running
  • A toilet visit is a sit, not a stand: the minion turns its back to the bowl, its body bends into an L of torso, thighs and shins on the seat with the tank behind, shuffles on the seat now and then, straightens and stands up as the visit's last second runs out, and the bowl flickers water-blue behind it. The legs are boxes every figure carries unseen until it sits; the pixel patch rides along, lower, over the lap. The bowl's spot is one helper the fixture and the sitter both use. All on the order's own clock, no timers of its own
  • A carrier that gives up sets the crate down behind it, on the way it came, never in the way ahead; the wedged-carrier scenario is back and checks what the rule promises, that the retry goes to somebody else, not that the crate lands past a body frozen in a storage row
  • A lounger's next thing may be picked from its bubble: a row of five pixel glyphs under the words, a barbell, a bed, a book, a nozzle and a bowl, each in its own flat colour, drawn in code. A click gives the order through the calls the idle clock makes, takeTurnInGym, visitBath with showering set, or send to the lounge or the dorm, and hands the minion a fresh idle clock. The row is dimmed and clicks do nothing while a job is in hand, one waits, a crate is carried, or the minion is at work or mid-visit. The overlay gets first say on hovers and clicks, so the bubble stays while the mouse is over it; the hit rects are kept under a lock for the main thread. STATION.md: one line under the lounge rules
  • Headless runs never take the keyboard: the model-only tests and a snapshot run as a background app like the scenario suite already did
  • One rule for walkers meeting: drift a third of a tile to the side away from the other, pass, drift back onto the line, the other doing the same; hold still where there is no room, an arm's length off someone standing on the walk's last spot. Gone: right of way, the wait-then-replan, the third-of-a-tile yield, the idle bystander's step-aside, the doorway lanes and their claims, the replan throttle for meetings (the floor-change one stays). Walk.swift is SceneKit-free and --walk-tests runs it on made-up bodies; the wedged-carrier scenario is dropped, since it only passed by letting a walker slide onto an occupied spot. STATION.md's walking rules say the one rule
  • The scenario suite is a smoke set again: ten scenarios that pinned incidents fixed days ago are gone (two source-lag cases the ledger tests cover, five walking and carrying incidents, three visit-length checks the soak still makes), fourteen flows remain and the gate runs in fifteen seconds. Visits last minutes, not seconds: a shower two to three, the toilet one, a gym turn four to eight, a look round two to four
  • A visit carries its length on the order, so a bath or a gym turn that waited its turn in pending still lasts once there: the sub-second shower was begin() zeroing a length set after start(). Bathers and exercisers face their fixture, not the camera; the bench presser lies along the bench; nobody hops in the shower; the pixel pants are wider and coarser; the nozzle sits clear of a head with the drops under it. Body: the simulation's side of a minion as a SceneKit-free base class, Minion the figure on it
  • A headless scenario run skips what only the eye reads: the view's tick (camera, labels, HUD) and the airlock pane's opening, which decide nothing and were a third of every tick; couch and bed spots are built once per floor plan, not once per resting minion per tick. The look-round scenario goes from 6.8 s to 1.7 s
  • The idle pick and the doorway lanes as rules apart from the picture: IdleClock, IdlePick and RoamSpots in Idle.swift, DoorLanes and LaneClaims in Lanes.swift, no SceneKit in either; the scene calls them; --idle-tests and --lane-tests run them against a hand-stepped clock and made-up bodies
  • Idle life that lasts: a visit's time starts on arrival; one idle clock per lounger picks a roam, a gym turn, the bath or the couch; doorways are one-lane sections with claims on the station clock; walkers who block each other resolve by right of way; re-planning throttled to once a second; scenario waits in station seconds with the idle soak off the default gate; model-only idle and lane tests; a fast local build mode; TESTING.md with the plan for model-only tests and the model-from-picture split
  • Truth-state work in progress as found on the branch: doorway lanes with claims that lapse, one idle clock per lounger with a weighted pick, visits timed from arrival, gym and roam scenarios, and TESTING.md, the spec for what follows

• A repository whose merges deploy ships on merge: detected from no release history and a workflow deploying on push to its trunk, or said in .github/rumkapsel.json; the merged crate goes to storage and straight up in a small rocket of its own, and its rows are forgotten when it climbs, since no source will ever say it shipped; the verbose scenario dump shows rockets and ledger rows
  • A repository's release pipeline is read from its release history, where most work lands, where releases end and what is released onward, with the rarer merge direction taken as a back-merge; branch names are the fallback; .github/rumkapsel.json overrides both for everyone; the Releases tab shows each repository's pipeline and why; model-only pipeline tests
  • Sharing shows more and clutters less: only offices worked in within twelve hours are shared; a shared office carries its pull request and checks and its sessions' life, drawn as real minions with their cones; a peer's local office someone works in is solid with its outline as a mark, and an idle one is dimmed; peer figures leave with their peer; the snapshot keeps its version so 0.27 peers still read it
  • Every repository has its own way to production, read from its branches: trunk develop or main, staging only where it exists, production or master or main; releases from the trunk, staging, or a release or hotfix branch; a repository without staging loads its rocket from storage and its yard comes from git unless it uses the board's middle columns; the shuttle check counts only a ship down over its slot
  • Hold space to run the station at four times speed: station time is stepped apart from the view, so walks stay walks and the camera stays on real time; a cue in the HUD while it is held, and a lost focus lets go
  • A teammate's reaction ends before rest or the next reaction moves the body: the ownership rule had refused both, leaving teammates reacting from bed
  • A relaunch takes the source's word again: a hand move from before is history, except aboard the rocket
  • A source that changes its mind while a crate is on its way stands over the landing: the ledger remembers the yard an order was made against, so a board move during a haul is carried on after it lands rather than buried under the station's newer move; ledger rows in the state dump
  • A rocket is loaded from the front: the crate aims at the tile before its own rocket's hull and the rocket is an obstacle, walked round, never through; whoever yields right of way steps aside where no way round exists; a chore never stands in a doorway; a verbose scenario and a simulator snapshot dump every body
  • A crate is a task: an office's package takes the issue its pull request closes, the pull request's own number when it closes none; the link is learned from every pull request answer and the board and kept with the board; git's release cargo is translated to tasks on the floor; a crate's hover lists its pull requests and its click opens the task
  • Any timed phase is steady, a teammate's reaction included; someone on a couch or in bed is off the walkway and in nobody's way; a given-up reaction ends the way a reaction ends
  • A delivery is picked up, period: a new office's crate is an order by number shared by the shuttle, the floor and the carrier, so an office renamed while its ship is in the air is still walked in; a crate on the bay floor with nobody fetching goes to the next free hands and folds away only if its office is gone; a bay slot is free only when nothing lies on it; named waits give up after ninety station seconds; bodies solid by default; a state dump on SIGUSR1
  • A job queued behind a rest survives the next rest re-plan, and begins the moment a worker is out of the shuttle
  • The board's delta asks every not-shipped item by number, since a move on the board never touches the issue's own timestamp and the search missed every move; the running station writes station.log in Application Support: events, commands, give-ups and GitHub asks
  • The counters and titles count your sessions only, not teammates, subagents or freed workers; options to hide the private station and the repository titles; the GitHub interval explained as the backstop it is
  • One owner per body and a body reconciler: the command in hand owns place, path and pose, and send refuses anything else; a body standing still ten seconds in a phase that should move, waiting on nothing named, gives up and says so; a given-up carry goes back in the queue from where the crate lies, an office crate back on the bay list for the next free hands; deliveries are a queue; right of way when two meet; a scenario fails on an unexpected give-up; rockets standing by and due rings follow the pad when the floor grows
  • A visit lasts its whole time: a session refresh no longer re-plans a bather's or a chore's rest under them; the shuttle holds over its slot until the carrier stands beside it; a floor change re-plans a fetch to the crate, not at random; a minion standing still mid-command for ten seconds says so in the log
  • Two can pass on one tile, never through each other: a body is solid at its tile's middle, the way past runs along the edge; room rules written down: one doorway kept clear, fixtures along the walls, the sign in the far corner
  • Nothing sits in a doorway: beds keep off the dorm's door cell and the bath's fixtures off its door and sign; a walk whose only way is past someone waits on them instead of finding no way; the Bath press picks like the Workout press
  • The Workout press takes whoever is resting: a lounger first, then a quiet worker still counted busy, then a sleeping teammate; a turn in the gym is not cut short by a session refresh re-planning rest
  • Faster feedback from GitHub: the board's delta, the feed as a doorbell, asks that expect a change
  • The gym: a room off the living cluster, four fixtures, a turn that lasts its whole time
